## Summary
A bulk export is a mass PHI disclosure path and an availability risk. It must be restricted, asynchronous, audited and preferably de-identified.

## Findings
| id | severity | category | location | evidence | recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARC-001 | critical | security | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/config/SecurityConfig.java:44 | Under the current matcher any CLINICIAN could call a new `/fhir/$export` | Restrict $export to ADMIN or a dedicated EXPORT role, with human approval per export run. |
| ARC-002 | high | performance | context/standards/api-standards.md:10 | A synchronous response containing every Patient and Observation is unbounded and ties up a request thread and a DB connection for minutes | Asynchronous pattern: `202 Accepted` + `Content-Location` status URL; write NDJSON to storage in chunks; throttle. |
| ARC-003 | medium | security | sample-app/src/main/java/org/example/fhir/audit/AuditLogger.java:17 | AuditLogger has no export action | Add `Action.EXPORT` and record each export through AuditLogger with counts only. |
| ARC-004 | high | security | context/security/phi-and-secrets-policy.md:7 | Research use of identified PHI needs a legal basis | Default to a de-identified export; identified export only with documented approval. |

## Decisions
- Recommend a de-identified, asynchronous export run by an ADMIN-approved job; ADR-0002 draft included.

## Open questions
- Is identified data actually required by research, or is de-identified data enough?
